Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

networkflow 0.0.9.9004 (2026-11-05)

Fifth step: a second rule to follow clusters across windows, a clearer name for the naming of dynamic clusters, and a better order for alluvial plots.

Breaking changes

  • merge_dynamic_clusters() has a required method: "majority" (the double majority, the only rule so far) or "jaccard" (new, see below). threshold_similarity has no default any more (it used to be 0.5001): the rule, its threshold and the type of similarity change the dynamic clusters, so all three must be given. Calls of earlier versions need method = "majority" and a threshold.
  • merge_diagnostics() has a required method too, and thresholds is NULL by default (a grid for each rule); its result has a method column.
  • networks_to_alluv() returns window as a factor whose levels follow the order of the list: windows with numeric names (“2”, “10”) are no longer sorted alphabetically in the table and in the plot.

New features

  • merge_dynamic_clusters(method = "jaccard"): overlap matching with a Jaccard threshold, as in the tracking of dynamic communities of Greene et al. (2010). Candidate pairs have a Jaccard index of at least the threshold (which can be well below 0.5); they are taken by decreasing index, each past identifier going to one cluster at most. similarity_type = "partial" restricts the union to the nodes present in both windows. With verbose = TRUE, the function says which rule it applies. merge_diagnostics() and plot_merge_diagnostics() work with both rules, and the guide “Following clusters over time” compares them.
  • minimize_crossing_alluvial() refines its order against the crossings of the flows themselves (refine = TRUE, max_passes): on the stagflation data, the weighted crossings fall from about 380 to 90. It reports the crossings before and after (verbose).
  • name_clusters(): name_merged_clusters is renamed name_dynamic_clusters (the old name still works, with a deprecation warning).

Bug fixes

  • minimize_crossing_alluvial() pasted the numbers of the components into a string to sort the clusters, which mixed “1” “10” and “11” “0” as soon as there were ten components or more.

Documentation

  • The guide “Following clusters over time” discusses the risk of building communities of documents of the same years rather than thematic communities on a long period (coupling, and possibly co-citation), says that windows must overlap (window_step smaller than time_window, not only window_step = 1) for documents to be matched, and presents the multislice community detection and the significance-clustered alluvial maps as possible future methods.
  • The README lists the study of Boucher and Fan (2025) among those that used the package.

networkflow 0.0.9.9003 (2026-11-04)

Fourth step: one method to build networks, and the Shiny application moves to its own package.

Breaking changes

  • build_network() and build_dynamic_networks(): a single argument, method, replaces projection_method, cooccurrence_method and model. There is no default, so that the choice stays explicit. The similarity measures of biblionetwork are "angle", "strength", "similarity", "jaccard" and "vladutz" (formerly "coupling_angle"…); the statistical backbones of the backbone package are "sdsm", "fdsm", "fixedfill", "fixedrow" and "fixedcol" (with alpha). Using the former arguments gives an error that shows the translation, for example projection_method = "structured", cooccurrence_method = "coupling_angle" becomes method = "angle".
  • launch_network_app() is removed from networkflow: the application moves to the package networkflowapp. shiny, DT, ggiraph and shinycssloaders are no longer suggested.

New features

  • layout_networks() has two new layouts: "forceatlas2" (the layout of Gephi, Jacomy et al., 2014, in a compact implementation) and "umap" (UMAP of McInnes et al., 2018, computed with uwot on the shortest-path distances of the network). The package uwot is suggested.
  • A new guide, “Drawing networks”, explains what a layout does, compares the layouts, and covers colours, labels and plot_networks(); this part of “Finding and reading clusters” is moved there. In “Finding and reading clusters”, the table of cluster sizes is a labelled tibble, the CPM example uses the density of the network as the scale of the resolution, name_clusters() is shown with a centrality ("tidygraph_functions"), and the interpretation of clusters cites Delcey et al.
  • With verbose = TRUE (now also the default of build_network()), the functions say which method they apply, what it measures and where it comes from (Sen and Gan, Shen et al., Neal…). The details of build_dynamic_networks() document the origin of each method.

networkflow 0.0.9.9002 (2026-11-04)

Third step of the development: alignment with biblionetwork 0.2.0, a lighter installation, clearer entry functions and documentation, and a new README and website theme (changes of 2026-11-02 to 2026-11-04).

Breaking changes

  • build_dynamic_networks() now stops when time_variable or time_window is missing, instead of silently building the single network of build_network(): that was not what a user calling a “dynamic” function meant. The error says to use build_network() and suggests the columns that look like a time variable (dates, or numbers named like a year). build_network() is unchanged.

New features

  • All the similarity measures of biblionetwork 0.2.0 are available in cooccurrence_method: "coupling_jaccard" and "coupling_vladutz" join "coupling_angle", "coupling_strength" and "coupling_similarity". The edges are computed with biblionetwork::biblio_coupling(method = ), and document_id (entity coupling) accepts the five measures through biblionetwork::entity_network() (it used to refuse "coupling_similarity").
  • plot_alluvial() accepts the list of graphs with dynamic clusters directly (it calls networks_to_alluv()), and min_share_cluster and min_windows_cluster keep the main clusters only: the whole alluvial workflow in one call. The separate functions remain available.

Lighter installation

  • ggalluvial and tidytext are moved from Imports to Suggests, with lifecycle (only used to write the documentation), and forcats, stringr and stopwords, which the package barely used, are removed: 16 packages are imported instead of 22. plot_alluvial(), extract_tfidf() and name_clusters(method = "tf-idf") ask to install ggalluvial or tidytext when they are needed (rlang::check_installed()).

Documentation and website

  • build_dynamic_networks() and build_network() document, case by case, which arguments to choose (coupling, backbone, one network per period, co-citation, authors, other two-mode tables) and what each projection_method uses and ignores.
  • The five measures are described, with their formulas, in the documentation and in the first guide, and linked to the explanations of biblionetwork. The first guide compares the coupling angle, the Jaccard index and the coupling similarity, and shows how much a statistical backbone prunes a network, with the numbers of nodes and edges of a coupling angle network.
  • The formulas of the function documentation are displayed on the website (KaTeX), and the footer names the two maintainers.
  • The README is written in Quarto (README.qmd); its illustration comes in a light and a dark version that follow the theme of the website. It mentions the Digital History of Macroeconomics project.
  • Package names are written in code font, with a link at first mention, in the documentation and the guides.
  • New site theme, logo and favicons.

Other changes

  • biblionetwork >= 0.2.0 is required (biblio_coupling() is the general function; coupling_entity() is deprecated in favour of entity_network()), which also fixes the coupling similarity (the idf-weighted cosine of Shen et al., 2019) and the weights of the coupling strength.
  • The Authors@R field of DESCRIPTION is fixed (a missing comma).

networkflow 0.0.9.9001 (2026-11-01)

Second step: the pipeline is generalised beyond bibliographic coupling, and time windows are reworked.

Breaking changes

  • build_dynamic_networks(): overlapping_window is replaced by window_step, the number of units between the starts of two windows (window_step = 1 replaces overlapping_window = TRUE; by default, windows follow each other). Using overlapping_window gives an error that says so.
  • build_dynamic_networks(): the arguments are reordered (data, entities, projection, time, options) and ... only accepts the arguments of filter_components(): a misspelt argument is now an error instead of being ignored. build_network() follows the same order.
  • Windows of a single time unit are named after the unit ("1990", "2001-Q2") instead of "1990-1990".
  • plot_networks() returns a named list of ggplot objects for a list of graphs (it used to store the plots in the graphs, in an element plot).
  • The research scripts that call build_dynamic_networks(overlapping_window = TRUE) must use window_step = 1.

New features

  • Dates and finer time units: time_variable can be a Date, a POSIXct or an ISO date written as text, and time_unit ("year", "quarter", "month", "week", "day") sets the unit in which time_window and window_step are counted. The time column of the user is not modified.
  • merge_diagnostics() and plot_merge_diagnostics() show how the dynamic clusters change with the threshold and the type of similarity of merge_dynamic_clusters() (number of clusters, lifespans, share of nodes in persistent clusters).
  • add_node_roles() documents how to read each role, with examples from the stagflation data, and the guide shows how roles change with the resolution. Running add_node_roles() again replaces the earlier roles instead of duplicating the columns.
  • The guides cite the literature on direct citation (Klavans and Boyack, Waltman and van Eck, Rivest et al., Sjögårde and Ahlgren, Kleminski et al.) and discuss other ways to follow clusters over time (Jaccard matching, multislice community detection, significance-clustered alluvial maps).
  • Figures of the guides open in a lightbox.
  • Co-citation: build_network() and build_dynamic_networks() gain projection_on = "target", which links the target_id entities that share source_id entities (e.g. cited works linked when cited together).
  • time_in = "edges": the time variable can be a column of the table of links (e.g. the year of the citing document), so that windows follow the citing documents (co-citation) or the documents of entities without a date (authors). Successive windows can then be matched, since nodes persist.
  • document_id: coupling of entities that publish documents (authors, journals, institutions), counting the documents that cite each reference, through biblionetwork::entity_network().
  • compute_size counts the citing documents of each node when the nodes are linked through their own links (co-citation, time_in = "edges").
  • A fourth guide, “Beyond bibliographic coupling”, shows co-citation, author coupling and co-authorship, and explains why the identifiers of references matter.
  • Windows without any edge give an empty network (with a warning) that filter_components(), add_clusters() and the following steps accept; nodes or links with a missing time are dropped with a warning (they used to make the function fail).

networkflow 0.0.9.9000 (2026-11-01)

First step: rewrite of the documentation and of the code of the former GitHub version (0.0.9), with tests and benchmarks. To be released on CRAN as 0.1.0.

Breaking changes

  • merge_dynamic_clusters(): similarity_type must be given ("complete" or "partial"). Its former default could not be used anyway (it failed with “the condition has length > 1”).
  • add_clusters(): cluster identifiers are numbered by decreasing size for every algorithm (“01” is the largest cluster). Leiden identifiers were previously in the order returned by igraph: partitions are unchanged, but labels may differ from those obtained with an earlier version.
  • add_clusters(): Louvain, fast greedy, walktrap and Infomap now use the weight edge column, as documented. Through tidygraph, they used to ignore it (only Leiden used the weights): partitions obtained with these algorithms on weighted networks change.
  • build_network(): model, alpha and backbone_args are explicit arguments; ... only goes to filter_components().
  • build_dynamic_networks() keeps node_size computed by compute_size instead of duplicating an existing node_size column.

Removed

  • The deprecated functions are removed: community_colors(), community_labels(), community_names(), dynamic_network_cooccurrence(), intertemporal_cluster_naming(), leiden_workflow(), tbl_main_component() and top_nodes(). Use color_networks(), prepare_label_networks(), name_clusters(), build_dynamic_networks(), merge_dynamic_clusters(), add_clusters() and filter_components().

Other changes

  • add_clusters(): the default of n_iterations is now -1 (Leiden iterates until the partition is stable) instead of 1000. Results are close but not identical to those obtained with 1000 iterations, and much faster on large networks.
  • launch_network_app(): the UI, the server and the plot are now separate internal functions, tested with shiny::testServer(); the default layout is "fr" (Kamada-Kawai reads similarity weights as distances).
  • citation("networkflow") works (inst/CITATION).
  • Credits: Alexandre Truc initiated the alluvial method; Thomas Delcey and Aurélien Goutsmedt maintain the package.
  • GitHub Actions: an R-CMD-check workflow (three systems) was added, and the pkgdown workflow installs Quarto.

Bug fixes

  • add_node_roles() computed the within-module degree and the participation coefficient wrongly for the node at the to end of each edge: all its ties were counted as internal to its cluster. Roles computed with earlier versions should be recomputed.
  • add_clusters(seed = ) no longer changes the random-number stream of the session: the seed is set locally with withr::local_seed() (CRAN policy).
  • add_clusters() returns an error instead of NULL for an input that is neither a tbl_graph nor a list of them.
  • add_clusters() and merge_dynamic_clusters() return graphs with the node table active (they left the edge table active).
  • merge_dynamic_clusters() can be run again on graphs that already have dynamic clusters, works on unnamed lists and on graphs whose edges lack the *_from/*_to cluster columns, and warns when consecutive windows share no node (successive windows of documents cannot be matched).
  • build_network(projection_method = "statistical", filter_components = TRUE) failed with “unused arguments”.
  • build_dynamic_networks() no longer fails on a window where no target is shared by two sources (it returns a graph without edges).
  • name_clusters(method = "given_column", name_merged_clusters = TRUE) failed; the check that tidygraph was attached (through sessionInfo()) is removed.
  • prepare_label_networks() ignored x and y for a single graph.
  • plot_networks(print_plot_code = TRUE) used a wrong title for lists.
  • filter_components() and layout_networks() returned their result invisibly.
  • layout_networks() no longer triggers ggraph’s warning about existing x and y columns.
  • extract_tfidf() no longer triggers data.table’s “shallow copy” warning, and missing texts no longer produce the term “na”.
  • color_networks(): with more than 14 categories, the default palette used 13 colours; it now uses 14 and warns that colours are recycled.

networkflow 0.0.9

Development version, distributed from GitHub (it was numbered 1.0.0).

Deprecated and new functions:

  • dynamic_network_cooccurrence() is deprecated and is replaced by build_dynamic_networks();
  • tbl_main_component() is deprecated and is replaced by build_network() and filter_components();
  • leiden_workflow() is deprecated and is replaced by add_clusters();
  • community_names() is deprecated and is replaced by name_clusters();
  • community_colors() is deprecated and is replaced by color_networks();
  • intertemporal_cluster_naming() is deprecated and is replaced by merge_dynamic_clusters();
  • A new function computes coordinates with different layout algorithms: layout_networks().
